original_value: Aggregation operators are important tools for solving multi-attribute group decision-making (MAGDM) problems. The main challenging issue for aggregating data in a MAGDM problem is how to develop a symmetric aggregation operator expressing the decision makers’ behavior. In the literature, there are some methods dealing with this difficulty; however, they lack an effective approach for multi-polar inputs. In this study, a new aggregation operator for m-polar fuzzy soft sets (M-pFSMWM) reflecting different agreement scenarios within a group is presented to proceed MAGDM problems in which both attributes and experts have different weights. Moreover, some desirable properties of M-pFSMWM operator, such as idempotency, monotonicity, and commutativity (symmetric), that means being invariant under any permutation of the input arguments, are studied. Further, m-polar fuzzy soft induced ordered weighted average (M-pFSIOWA) operator and m-polar fuzzy soft induced ordered weighted geometric (M-pFSIOWG) operator, which are extensions of IOWA and IOWG operators, respectively, are developed. Two algorithms are also designed based on the proposed operators to find the final solution in MAGDM problems with weighted multi-polar fuzzy soft information. Finally, the efficiency of the proposed methods is illustrated by some numerical examples. The characteristic comparison of the proposed aggregation operators shows the M-pFSMWM operator is more adaptable for solving MAGDM problems in which different cases of agreement affect the final outcome.

result.paraphrase: Aggregation operators are key tools for addressing multi-attribute group decision-making (MAGDM) problems. A central difficulty in MAGDM data aggregation is designing a symmetric operator that captures the behavior of decision makers. Although several approaches have been proposed in the literature, they do not provide an effective solution for multi-polar inputs. This study introduces a new aggregation operator for m-polar fuzzy soft sets (M-pFSMWM) that reflects different agreement scenarios within a group, enabling MAGDM problems where both attributes and experts carry different weights to be handled. In addition, the operator’s desirable properties, including idempotency, monotonicity, and commutativity (symmetry), meaning invariance under any permutation of the input arguments, are examined. Furthermore, m-polar fuzzy soft induced ordered weighted average (M-pFSIOWA) and m-polar fuzzy soft induced ordered weighted geometric (M-pFSIOWG) operators, as extensions of the IOWA and IOWG operators, respectively, are developed. Two algorithms based on the proposed operators are also designed to obtain the final solution in MAGDM problems with weighted multi-polar fuzzy soft information. Finally, numerical examples are used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods. The comparative analysis of the proposed aggregation operators indicates that the M-pFSMWM operator is more adaptable for MAGDM problems in which varying agreement cases influence the final outcome.
